skill.name: geo-database
skill.description: Access NCBI GEO gene expression and genomics datasets, including GSE, GSM, GPL, SOFT, matrix, and supplementary files.
skill.summary: Search, download, and analyze NCBI GEO gene expression datasets.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documentation-heavy GEO database helper with many examples for public NCBI APIs, GEOparse, FTP downloads, and local file caching. Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, official URLs, biomedical identifiers, and Python .keys() usage. Remaining confirmed issues are expected but real risks from plaintext FTP recommendations, local file writes, and user-run shell commands.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS download links when available, and advise users to verify file checksums or provenance for bulk GEO downloads.

remediation.issue: Local file and directory writes in examples
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to choose an explicit project data directory, check available disk space, and avoid running examples in sensitive directories.

remediation.issue: Shell command examples for package installation and downloads
remediation.suggestion: Keep commands visible and explicit, and recommend reviewing package names and download destinations before execution.

content.value_statement: Finding usable GEO datasets can require many searches, formats, and access methods. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through GEO search, download, parsing, and analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains GEO accession types such as GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS, and Profiles.
Provides Entrez and GEOparse examples for searching and retrieving GEO metadata.
Shows how to download SOFT, matrix, MINiML, and supplementary files.
Demonstrates expression matrix extraction, filtering, and metadata inspection.
Outlines basic quality control, differential expression, clustering, and meta-analysis workflows.
Documents NCBI rate limits, API key setup, file sizes, and citation practices.
limitations: It is guidance and examples, not a complete validated analysis pipeline.
Large GEO files may require significant disk space and time to download.
Dataset quality depends on submitter metadata and platform annotation accuracy.
Users must confirm statistical assumptions before using results in research.

use_cases.title: Find disease expression studies
use_cases.description: Search GEO for human disease datasets and inspect study metadata before analysis.

use_cases.title: Build a transcriptomics workflow
use_cases.description: Download GEO series files, parse expression matrices, and prepare data for downstream statistics.

use_cases.title: Teach GEO data formats
use_cases.description: Explain SOFT, MINiML, series matrix, platform annotation, and accession hierarchy using concrete examples.

prompt_templates.title: Search for a dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the geo-database skill to find GEO studies about breast cancer in Homo sapiens. Explain the search terms and summarize promising GSE accessions.

prompt_templates.title: Download and inspect a series
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the geo-database skill to show how I can download GSE123456 with GEOparse, inspect sample metadata, and find the expression matrix.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare differential expression inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the geo-database skill to outline a workflow for comparing control and treated samples from a GEO series. Include quality checks and required metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a cross-study meta-analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the geo-database skill to design a meta-analysis across several GEO series for one gene. Include platform mapping, batch concerns, and reproducibility steps.

output_examples.input: Find GEO datasets for human diabetes RNA-seq studies.
output_examples.output: A ranked search plan with Entrez query terms, organism filters, likely GEO accession types, and metadata fields to review before downloading.

output_examples.input: Help me inspect a GEO series matrix file.
output_examples.output: Step-by-step guidance for loading the matrix, checking sample columns, reviewing platform annotations, and identifying expression value scale.

output_examples.input: Compare expression of TP53 across three GEO studies.
output_examples.output: A meta-analysis outline covering dataset retrieval, probe-to-gene mapping, per-study summary statistics, and warnings about platform differences.

best_practices: Set an Entrez email and respect NCBI rate limits when using programmatic access.
Inspect sample metadata, platform annotation, and processing methods before analysis.
Cache downloaded data in a dedicated directory and record accessions for reproducibility.
anti_patterns: Do not combine studies without checking batch effects and platform compatibility.
Do not assume expression values are normalized or log-transformed without reading metadata.
Do not download large supplementary files before confirming disk space and relevance.

faq.question: What is NCBI GEO?
faq.answer: NCBI GEO is a public repository for gene expression and functional genomics datasets from many experimental platforms.

faq.question: Does this skill download data automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and code examples that users can review before downloading public GEO data.

faq.question: What accession types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Series, Samples, Platforms, DataSets, and Profiles, commonly identified by GSE, GSM, GPL, and GDS accessions.

faq.question: Can it analyze RNA-seq and microarray data?
faq.answer: It provides workflow guidance for both, but users must validate methods for each dataset and platform.

faq.question: Why does it mention API keys?
faq.answer: NCBI API keys are optional and increase E-utilities rate limits. The skill uses placeholder text, not real keys.

faq.question: What should I verify before using results?
faq.answer: Verify sample groups, normalization, platform annotation, batch effects, file provenance, and the original study citation.
